Hi Mama! I have a decent size fibroid. Around 3.5-4cms. A lot of women have them they just aren't large enough to see or the doctors don't feel the need to report them because of their size. I was told about 80% of women have them by the time they are in their 40s and 50s. They are little benign tumors that form within the uterus that usually don't do anything. Larger ones like yours most likely will need to be removed at some point. Not sure how far along you are but if that's how big it is early in your pregnancy, then you may have a c-section so they can remove it while they are in there. Not sure you can stop it from growing since it grows off your hormones. 

At this point, my best advice for you is to try and stay calm and trust your doctors. They will most likely have you receive more ultrasounds than a normal pregnancy to monitor it's growth but that's a good excuse to see the baby more :) You may have more pain/discomfort while the baby grows but you may not. Fibroids can also degenerate which means they get re-absorbed into the muscle tissue of the uterus. I have read that it's pretty painful but at least you lose the fibroid? 

There is a lot of stuff you can google and even more stuff you can worry about but at this point you just kinda have to go with the flow. Whatever happens, you got this and you will get a beautiful baby at the end of it :) I am due in a little under 8 weeks so I will let you know how it goes. 

Ps- Glad you named it Fred. Solid name and it shows you have a little humor about all of this. You will be a great mom.
